$comment: Classification rows (REQUIREMENTS #561, #562): ONE generic mechanism for every classification -- asset type, asset subtype, the component of findings and assets, and every later dimension (dimensions.locked.json holds only each dimension's values). A row = source (the provider whose naming it normalises) + field (an SI field, or a source path) + match (equals | in -> values; prefix | pattern -> pattern, a glob) -> target (the SI field it sets) = set, with a priority (an integer 0..10000, higher wins) and a state (enabled | disabled); an optional when (SI fields only) must also hold. Evaluated with the condition engine of the risk factors (engine/data-model/SI-Classification.ps1, tri-state: an undecided field never matches). targets: per target field its dimension, whether it is on assets or findings, multi (an asset carries every matching value) and the fallback when no row matches -- never blank ($keep = the value the sources gave). verify = true: the source spelling the row matches is still to be confirmed on live rows. Customer changes: Pro = one cfg.ItemOverride per row (classification:<row id> -- override, disable or add); Community = classification.custom.json, per id.

rules.note: Azure SQL (logical server, database, managed instance); Exposure Graph fills si_azure_resource_type for the same resources.
The SQL IaaS registration of a VM (#562: Server / SQL Server).
Every App Service resource (sites, slots, plans, certificates, static sites); API connections are Integration (asset-type-azure-api-connection).
A public IP address resource is a Public IP, like the public IPs SI profiles itself (above the generic Network row).
Any other Azure SQL resource (firewall rules, elastic pools, ...) -- below the specific SQL rows.
Disks, extensions, availability sets, scale sets, images ... -- BELOW the virtual machine row (500), so a VM stays a Server.
An Azure resource no row names is Other -- never the raw ARM type: that stays in si_azure_resource_type (and si_asset_type_source).
Defender for Endpoint / Exposure Graph deviceType (value map device_type).
Defender / Exposure Graph device category, when the device type says nothing.
The operating system, when Defender gives no device type (a discovered, not onboarded device).
A device the sources say nothing about (no device type, category or known operating system) -- Unknown, never a guess.
Entra userType (value map identity_type_user).
Entra servicePrincipalType (value map identity_type_sp).

A directory group (the Exposure Graph's group nodes; value map identity_type_eg) -- a group is an identity of its own kind, never Other. Identities only: an Azure resource whose type name ends in 'group' is not a directory group.
An identity of a kind no row names (a group, a service account, a computer object) is Other -- its source kind stays in si_asset_type_source.
Below the Defender device type: a VM Defender reports as a workstation (a virtual desktop) stays Workstation.
ServiceNow database classes (cmdb_ci_db_mssql_instance, ...). Below every collected type: a machine Defender sees stays a Server.
A VM registered with the SQL IaaS extension (its microsoft.sqlvirtualmachine resource names the VM).

Defender for Endpoint: a server whose software inventory shows SQL Server (vendor/product, e.g. microsoft/sql_server_2019). Management Studio and the drivers alone do not count. The product spelling is to be confirmed on live rows.
Exposure Graph deviceRole (value map eg_device_roles: SqlServer / SQL -> sql_server).
A public IP SI profiles itself reads like the Azure public IP address resource.
Defender / Exposure Graph device subtype.
The operating system family, when no role names the device (servers, workstations, mobiles only).
A SQL subtype gives the asset the SQL component (#562). PostgreSQL / MySQL count as SQL: they are SQL databases; a customer who wants them apart overrides this row.
Every other Azure SQL resource (firewall rules, elastic pools, ...) is SQL too.
SQL Server installed (Defender software inventory, vendor/product). Management Studio and the ODBC / OLE DB drivers alone do not make an asset SQL.
Every device has an operating system.
Every asset that reports an operating system (an Azure VM).

Defender vulnerability management SoftwareName (and Exposure Graph / Shodan product names): SQL Server, Management Studio, Native Client, ODBC / OLE DB drivers, Reporting / Analysis / Integration Services.
A CPE naming a Microsoft SQL product (cpe:2.3:a:microsoft:sql_server...).
Microsoft Office / Microsoft 365 Apps products (vendor microsoft).
A recommendation whose category is SQL (Defender configuration ConfigurationCategory, Defender for Cloud category, Defender for SQL).
A recommendation whose subcategory is SQL (Defender configuration ConfigurationSubcategory, Defender for Cloud security issue).
A recommendation whose name is about SQL (e.g. Defender for Cloud "SQL servers should have an Azure Active Directory administrator provisioned").
A finding on an Azure SQL resource concerns SQL. A VM with SQL Server installed is NOT here: its OS findings stay OS.
Defender configuration ConfigurationCategory OS.
A finding on a public IP (open ports, exposed services).
Any other affected software.
#772 the ServiceNow sub-CI: an OS finding goes under the CI's OS sub-CI. Evaluated after si_component (the targets' order), so it reads the finding's own component.
#772 the ServiceNow sub-CI: a SQL finding goes under the CI's SQL sub-CI. Every other component goes to the fallback bucket (the dimension's default, Other).

#772 the source says no fix exists (si_fix_available false, or a fix text such as No fix). #906: also a finding that names no recommended update (no update name, no update id) and has no date to age it by (no fix release, no first-seen) -- no single update, the same rule as the key figures; Unknown is left only for an update whose month cannot be read.
#772 the fix was released (or, without one dated update, the finding was first detected) longer than SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays (default 30) before the collection.
#772 within SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays of the collection (exactly the threshold included): fixed in the monthly cycle.
